hero.lead: A nation of 5.6 million with forest across three quarters of its land, whose State Treasury puts gross borrowing for 2026 at about €44.7 billion.

capital.heading: Forests and readers, and every table full.

record.text: Gross central government borrowing requirement for 2026, about €44.7 billion, with net borrowing of €13.6 billion, as the State Treasury stated in November 2026
Central government debt at the end of October 2026, €35,846 a person; it was €187.7 billion, 66.7% of GDP, at the end of 2025
EU recovery and resilience grants under the plan approved by the Council on 29 October 2021; the Commission authorised the fourth payment on 12 May 2026
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Central government borrowing, 2026
register.detail: State Treasury · gross borrowing requirement about €44.7bn and net €13.6bn, as stated in November 2026 · €44.493bn gross in the second supplementary budget proposal of 3 June 2026
register.note: All the euro-denominated syndicated supply for 2026 is completed, the State Treasury says
register.text: The State Treasury funds the central government budget with benchmark bonds, other long-term bonds and Treasury bills; it puts the gross borrowing requirement for 2026 at about €44.7 billion and net borrowing at €13.6 billion. The borrowing funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Seven-year benchmark bond (3.300%, April 2033)
register.detail: State Treasury · priced 19 August 2026 · settled 26 August 2026 · due 15 April 2033 · coupon 3.300% · yield 3.310%, 15 bps over mid-swaps
register.note: An order book of over €11 billion from 120 investors
register.text: A new seven-year euro benchmark bond of €4 billion, syndicated through BNP Paribas, BofA Securities, Danske Bank, Deutsche Bank and J.P. Morgan. It funds the central government budget as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Ten-year benchmark bond (3.35%, September 2036)
register.detail: State Treasury · launched 9 April 2026 · due 15 September 2036 · coupon 3.35% · yield at issue 3.362% · second syndicated transaction of 2026
register.note: Reported in the State Treasury Quarterly Review Q2/2026 of 26 June 2026
register.text: A new ten-year euro benchmark bond of €4 billion, the second syndicated transaction of the year. It funds the central government budget as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Fifteen-year benchmark bond (3.550%, April 2041)
register.detail: State Treasury · priced 21 January 2026 · settled 28 January 2026 · due 15 April 2041 · coupon 3.550% · yield 3.586%, 47 bps over mid-swaps
register.note: An order book of €25 billion from more than 160 investors; the first syndicated issue of 2026
register.text: A new fifteen-year euro benchmark bond of €3 billion, syndicated through Barclays, BNP Paribas, Danske Bank, Deutsche Bank and J.P. Morgan. It funds the central government budget as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants · Council approval 29 October 2021 · amended 14 March 2023 and 8 December 2023 · fourth payment authorised 12 May 2026
register.note: Pre-financing of €271 million was paid; the Commission has made a preliminary assessment of the fifth payment request
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Finland, paid in instalments against milestones and targets; 52.3% of the plan supports climate objectives. Its measures include €371.8 million to clear the backlog in social and health services, which serves the health standard, and €90 million to reform the public employment services, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Joensuu social infrastructure (Public Sector Loan Facility)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250237 · signed 17 December 2025 · announced 26 June 2026 · with an €18M EU grant under the Public Sector Loan Facility
register.note: A €160 million programme, including €22 million from the City of Joensuu
register.text: An EIB loan to the City of Joensuu, with an €18 million EU grant from the Public Sector Loan Facility, one of the three pillars of the Just Transition Mechanism, to build and renovate schools, childcare centres and student housing and to improve cultural facilities. It serves the education and shelter standards in eastern Finland.

register.name: Schools and kindergartens, City of Turku
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 9 March 2026 · 25-year uncommitted credit facility · 11 comprehensive schools, five school-and-kindergarten facilities, three kindergartens and one vocational school
register.note: Co-finances the construction and renovation of twenty education buildings
register.text: A 25-year NIB credit facility to the City of Turku to co-finance the construction and renovation of schools and kindergartens. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Laakso Hospital, second phase
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 20 November 2025 · additional request · borrower Laakso Joint Hospital · Helsinki
register.note: For patients in the Helsinki metropolitan area and beyond
register.text: A CEB loan that partly finances the second phase of the reconstruction of the Laakso Hospital area in Helsinki, including the main hospital, tunnels and a forensic psychiatric facility. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Hospital modernisation, Helsinki University Hospital (HUS)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 13 June 2025 · part of a €300M package · Meilahti (Helsinki), Jorvi (Espoo) and Peijas (Vantaa)
register.note: Most of the hospital works in Uusimaa are due to be finished at the end of 2026
register.text: The first EIB agreement in a €300 million package with Helsinki University Hospital, to modernise hospital buildings for better access to specialist care, better medical training and lower energy use. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Schools and learning facilities, City of Vantaa
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 13 June 2025 · part of a €350M package · more than 30 facilities and 160,000 m²
register.note: Over 11,000 pupils are expected to benefit; works planned over five years
register.text: An EIB loan for new and renovated schools, preschools and sports halls in Vantaa, part of a €350 million package. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Laakso Joint Hospital, finance contract
register.detail: European Investment Bank · finance contract announced 18 November 2024 · first instalment of up to €480M approved · total cost €1,011M
register.note: The CEB (€150 million) and Municipality Finance (€50 million) also lend to the project
register.text: The first instalment of EIB financing for the Laakso Joint Hospital, which will provide psychiatric and somatic care in the Laakso Hospital area in Helsinki and in Ohkola, Mäntsälä. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Assi central hospital, Hämeenlinna
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 24 April 2024 · 25-year uncommitted credit facility · Wellbeing Services County of Kanta-Häme · total cost about €460M
register.note: The 97,000 m² hospital is scheduled to become operational in November 2026
register.text: A 25-year NIB credit facility of up to €100 million to the Wellbeing Services County of Kanta-Häme for the new Assi hospital on the Ahvenisto hospital campus, for a county of about 170,000 people. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Steady Energy, heat-only small modular reactor
register.detail: European Investment Bank · announced 15 September 2026 · up to €40M · backed by InvestEU · research, testing and licensing in Finland, 2026–2028
register.note: A reactor designed to produce heat rather than electricity, for district heating networks
register.text: An EIB loan of up to €40 million to Steady Energy, backed by InvestEU, for the research, testing and licensing of its small modular reactor technology in Finland. It serves the energy standard with low-carbon heat for Finnish homes.

register.name: Atria convenience food factory, Nurmo
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 2 September 2026 · 10 years · modernisation and energy efficiency · operational in 2028
register.note: The upgrade electrifies key production processes and is expected to reduce the company’s Scope 1 and 2 emissions
register.text: A ten-year NIB loan to Atria Plc for a full refurbishment and modernisation of its convenience food factory in Nurmo, with energy efficiency improvements. It serves the food standard through food made in Finland, and the energy standard through lower energy use.

register.name: Y-Säätiö sustainability notes (4.875%, 2030)
register.detail: Y-Säätiö · issued 18 September 2025 · due 18 September 2030 · coupon 4.875% · issue price 99.593% · ISIN FI4000592209
register.note: Also refinances the €100 million notes of 2021 due 2026, of which €61.25 million were tendered and bought back
register.text: Five-year unsecured sustainability notes of a foundation that provides affordable rental homes and works to reduce homelessness, one of the key national developers of the Housing First principle in Finland. Its proceeds finance or refinance eligible assets under its Sustainability Bond Framework; it serves the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Pine, spruce and birch forest on the shore of a misty lake in the Finnish Lakeland, Finland

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: Clear blue lakes joined by a fast river among granite, pine and birch in the Finnish Lakeland, Finland

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A coastal wind farm by the Gulf of Bothnia, a solar park and power lines across pine forest in Finland

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: The tree-lined Esplanadi park walk in central Helsinki at golden hour, with pale stone buildings and people seen only far away, Finland

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.
items.alt: Harvested fields, red wooden farmhouses, pine forest and a calm lake in the Finnish countryside, Finland

items.name: Fiksuruoka
items.text: A Finnish online shop for rescued food that sells quality surplus and discontinued products at low prices, and since autumn 2025 has opened shops in Espoo, Vantaa and Turku; it says it has saved more than 23 million kilograms of food from waste.

items.name: ResQ Club
items.text: A Finnish app through which restaurants, cafés and shops sell surplus meals and groceries at a discount instead of throwing them away; with its users it has rescued more than 20 million items from waste.

items.name: Y-Säätiö (Y-Foundation)
items.text: A foundation that rents affordable homes and works to reduce homelessness, one of the key national developers of the Housing First principle in Finland; at the end of June 2026 its group owned 18,518 apartments in 55 municipalities, with rental income of €83.1 million in the first half of 2026.

items.name: Kontti recycling department stores
items.text: The second-hand department stores of the Finnish Red Cross, which sell donated goods to fund humanitarian work and offer supported employment through wage subsidies and work trials; in 2024 they operated in twelve cities, from Helsinki to Rovaniemi, and online.

items.name: Kierrätyskeskus (Helsinki Metropolitan Area Reuse Centre)
items.text: A non-profit founded in 1990 that runs second-hand shops and a nationwide online shop and employs long-term unemployed people as part of its business model; it circulates over 4 million products a year from 14 sites in Finland.
